title.value: Log meals and medical metrics into a health spreadsheet

introduction.value: A Claude Cowork skill tracks diet and medical metrics in a spreadsheet, and meals told to Claude on mobile are logged in the daily record.

method.value: The poster made a Claude Cowork “Health Related” folder on a desktop and asked Claude to create both a spreadsheet and a skill for tracking diet goals and medical metrics. After enabling Dispatch, they could tell Claude on their phone what they ate; Claude looked up nutrition on the web, split meals into line items, wrote protein/fat/carbs/calories into the .xlsx daily log, and also logged weight and blood pressure.

outcome.value: It produced per-item meal entries plus a running daily total against targets, then suggested how to use remaining calories and protein for later meals. The poster said setup took about eight minutes and described it as better than other tracking apps, but gave no longer-term results or accuracy checks.

notes.value: The main catch mentioned is format: Claude used an .xlsx file, and the poster had Excel on a Mac but was not sure whether Excel was required.

source_text.body:
Log meals and medical metrics into a health spreadsheet
A Claude Cowork skill tracks diet and medical metrics in a spreadsheet, and meals told to Claude on mobile are logged in the daily record.
Done with
CW
Claude Cowork
CL
Claude
What they did
The poster made a Claude Cowork “Health Related” folder on a desktop and asked Claude to create both a spreadsheet and a skill for tracking diet goals and medical metrics. After enabling Dispatch, they could tell Claude on their phone what they ate; Claude looked up nutrition on the web, split meals into line items, wrote protein/fat/carbs/calories into the .xlsx daily log, and also logged weight and blood pressure.
How it went
It produced per-item meal entries plus a running daily total against targets, then suggested how to use remaining calories and protein for later meals. The poster said setup took about eight minutes and described it as better than other tracking apps, but gave no longer-term results or accuracy checks.
Worth knowing
The main catch mentioned is format: Claude used an .xlsx file, and the poster had Excel on a Mac but was not sure whether Excel was required.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Cowork
Copy prompt
Set up a skill that tracks my diet and medical metrics such as [blood pressure, glucose, weight] in the spreadsheet at [file path]. When I tell you what I ate, log it with estimated [calories, protein, sodium] in today's row. When done, confirm the entry and show me the day's running totals.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCowork/comments/1sz5yqb/healthdiet_tracking_skill
